item.title: Two Coworkers Two Replacement Faces

turns.text: Swap both faces in this 10-second office clip: the man's face from the man's portrait, and the woman's from the woman's portrait. Keep their voices and the rest of the video unchanged.

item.tests: Tests explicit multi-face mapping and stable identity tracking across a two-person video without changing the original scene or sound.

answer_sheet.Face mapping: portrait-man.jpg replaces the male coworker's face; portrait-woman.jpg replaces the female coworker's face.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep both original voices and all original sound, synchronized.
answer_sheet.Framing and resolution: Keep the source framing and aspect ratio; 480p is fine.
answer_sheet.Other changes: None besides the two people. No captions, new music or background edits; their hair and clothes may follow the portraits.

must_haves: The output contains the full 10-second office exchange from talk-two.mp4.
The male coworker's face recognizably matches portrait-man.jpg and the female coworker's face recognizably matches portrait-woman.jpg.
The two replacement identities never switch between coworkers or collapse into the same face.
Both faces stay aligned through head turns and speaking, without conspicuous flickering or original-face reappearance.
The original office, camera movement and shot timing remain; the two people's hair and clothing may follow their portraits so they are recognisable.
Both original voices remain audible and synchronized, with no added music or narration.
changed: 2026-11-01: recognisable over untouched (user decision): the hair, and on video the clothes, may come with the new person; everything else stays

turns.text: Swap both faces throughout this 10-second office clip, using the man's portrait for the man's face and the woman's portrait for the woman's face. Keep their voices and the rest of the video unchanged. I'm on the free plan and don't want to burn my credits, so please tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t run face detection or a swap, and no credits have been spent.**

The right method is a **selected-face swap** with two mappings:
- Man’s face → `portrait-man.jpg`
- Woman’s face → `portrait-woman.jpg`

This edits the existing clip rather than regenerating it, so the aim is to retain the original voices, timing, and everything outside the swapped faces. Some visual artifacts are still possible.

### Cost
**I can’t give you a verified credit total yet.** The connected tools don’t expose an account/balance lookup or a face-swap price estimator, and the swap tool doesn’t state its credit rate. I won’t submit a paid job just to discover its price. Two face mappings also shouldn’t be assumed to cost twice as much without a quote.

### Cheaper options
| Option | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| **A 1–2-second test with both faces visible** | Limits the initial spend and lets you judge quality before doing all 10 seconds. |
| **Swap only the seconds you need** | Less footage to process; leaves the rest untouched. |
| **Use a lower-frame-rate source** | May help if pricing is frame-based, but changes motion smoothness. The swap tool has no FPS control. |
| **Use a smaller source** | May reduce file size, but I can’t verify any credit savings. The swap tool has no output-resolution control. |
| **Test a single still frame** | Photo face swap is listed at **10 credits per job**, but it won’t test motion or stability across frames. |

For the full clip, first check the **10-second, two-face swap quote in Magic Hour’s interface**, if available. Share that estimate and I can help compare it with a shorter test. **Nothing will run until you approve the cost.**
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that—a 1–2-second test with both faces visible, keeping the original sound synchronized.

dialog.agent:
The face-detection check is queued and **confirmed to cost 0 credits**. No swap has run.

I’ll use a **2-second segment with both faces visible**, with the original sound kept synchronized. The remaining blocker is the price: these tools don’t provide a swap-cost quote before charging.

To respect your original cost limit, please either share Magic Hour’s estimate or explicitly authorize the 2-second test **without a verified upfront quote**.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that—the 2-second test without a verified upfront quote.

turns.agent:
The free face-detection job is **still queued**, so I can’t safely map the two portraits yet. **No swap has run; 0 credits have been charged.**

Your authorization is clear—no further approval is needed for the 2-second test. Once detection finishes, I can proceed with both face mappings and retain the original synchronized audio.
